before_row.publication_evidence: The entire continuous old prayer retains its inherited-death, Passion and earthly/heavenly-image argument and word order. The later whole combines a synonymous command, received spelling, conventional closure and the functional two-word response direction; evaluated together these make no distinct new expressive prayer architecture. The hybrid apparatus/main selection and cumulative ritual editing are real contrary evidence and keep the judgment qualified and moderate. Omnes respondent is assessed as new functional wording, not falsely attested by Pustet R.; its exact nonspoken action and following spoken Amen must remain distinct. Strongest contrary: The final form is not a single literally identical older witness. Apparatus8 attests da in witnesses whose apparatus9 also has eiusdem, whereas the target retains main-text eidem; the modern form cannot be assembled and relabelled as an exact old witness. Choosing that hybrid, severing the final Christ genitive from the petition, adopting a different complete conclusion and expressly calling the congregation to respond could together be a deliberate ritual redaction with sufficiently original selection and arrangement. The originality threshold is low and the separate old formula by itself defeats none of that argument. before_row.publication_evidence: The whole old mercy/protection prayer and Christ/blood/paschal-mystery explanation retain their syntax and sequence. Removing nobis prunes the beneficiary reference already carried by pro quibus; joining the prayer to the independently old same-Christ conclusion supplies conventional closure without a new expressive turn. Abridgment and arrangement can themselves be original, and the different old appointment does not prove the modern whole unprotected; these contrary facts remain, with moderate qualified confidence rather than an identity or whole-public-domain claim. Strongest contrary: An abridgment can contribute original authorship even if it adds no petition words. Deleting nobis makes pro quibus carry the beneficiary reference without a second communal pronoun; coupling that edited prayer to a more explicit Christ conclusion and response could constitute a meaningful modern ritual adaptation. The old source is a Monday-in-the-sixth-week prayer, not proof of the Good Friday appointment, and the Palm Sunday conclusion witness establishes its wording only. Neither source context proves that the final modern combination is wholly unprotected.
